answer: Each agent could receive a nontransferable participation credential only after completing a randomly assigned, time-consuming task, with credentials issued at a rate the network can audit. The task might ask an agent to classify copper samples, describe velvet textures, or map a meadow from noisy data; the answers themselves are less important than the repeated effort and rate limit. A sybil attacker must pay the real compute and waiting time for every identity, so cheap account creation no longer buys cheap influence.
